It started about a year ago—which was roughly a year and a half after my promotion started going downhill—and it usually happens late at night when I'm alone in the office or my home office.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice is commanding you to do things, or is it more observational, just commenting on what you're doing without telling you what to do?\n\nPatient: It's definitely more observational; it doesn't command me to do things, but rather comments on what I am already doing. It just makes me feel like I'm operating on a completely different level of understanding than everyone else.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever questioned whether the voice you hear or the mission you believe in might not be real, or has there ever been a moment where you doubted your special role in this cyber threat protection?\n\nPatient: Even though I know there's physically nobody in the room when I hear that voice, I still believe in my gut that the threat and my mission are completely real. While I do regularly hear that metallic, echoey voice commenting on my actions, my experiences have never included any visual hallucinations.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where your thoughts or actions have become so disorganized or confusing that it's been hard for you to achieve your goals or complete tasks, even those related to your mission?\n\nPatient: Yes, my wife and coworkers say that when I try to explain my work, I jump rapidly from firewall rules to Bible verses to youth soccer drills, often trailing off mid-sentence. I also get easily distracted by blinking notifications or sudden ideas, meaning I'll start five different tasks at once but struggle to finish any of them.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how these distractions and rapid shifts in thought affect your ability to work on your mission, and do you feel like these experiences are part of the mission itself or separate from it?\n\nPatient: At first, I feel like this hyper-charged state with a dozen browser tabs open in my mind is part of how God specially wired me to handle this massive mission. Even during periods when my mood is completely flat—neither highly energized nor deeply depressed—I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe senior leadership is monitoring me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there was a specific event or period when your beliefs about the mission and the voice started to feel more real or intense, and how they have evolved over time in relation to your mood swings and irritability?\n\nPatient: They became most intense during the height of the migration chaos, about a year and a half after my promotion, when I was completely revved up, barely sleeping, and snapping at everyone. While the voice and my beliefs definitely peak during those highly energized, irritable phases, they still continue even during flatter periods when I'm not experiencing extreme mood swings.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the mission and the voice would change if someone were to provide you with undeniable proof that the cyber threat you're fighting doesn't exist and that the voice you hear is a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: Honestly, even if someone showed me what they call \"undeniable proof,\" I still know in my gut that this threat is very real. The voice and this mission feel way too real to dismiss, and I think others are just blind to what's actually going on.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there have been periods where your beliefs about the mission and the voice seemed to fade away or become less intense, or have they been consistently present since they started?\n\nPatient: They have actually been pretty consistent and haven't really faded away since they first started about a year and a half ago. Even during times when my mood is totally flat and I'm just going through the motions, I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe I'm being monitored. It has just become a regular, ongoing part of my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and interactions with others have changed since you started believing in this mission and hearing the voice, and have you noticed any impact on your relationships or work performance?\n\nPatient: It's had a huge impact—I've been written up at work, had key parts of my project taken away, and had to step down from coaching and church leadership. At home, my wife has taken over the parenting and bills because she doesn't trust my judgment or follow-through right now. I either end up snapping at people when they don't see my vision, or completely shutting down and ignoring everyone when I'm in a low phase.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how long you've had these beliefs about the mission and heard the voice without any significant breaks or periods where they completely stopped, and have you experienced any significant stressors or life changes around the time they started?\n\nPatient: The voice and my belief that I'm being monitored have been a regular, persistent part of my life for about a year and a half now without any real breaks. It all started after a major stressor about two and a half years ago when I was promoted to lead a high-stakes IT migration while simultaneously studying for my PMP and CISSP exams and keeping up a demanding church and coaching schedule.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period where you questioned the reality of your mission or the voice, or has there been any time when you felt like you were living in a dream or detached from reality?"

However, getting pulled away by minor distractions means I start five things and finish none, which really gets in the way of actually completing my work. It’s been incredibly frustrating because it has contributed to me getting written up and losing some of my key responsibilities at the office.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between the voice's comments, which seem to be about your actions and progress, and your own thoughts, especially when you're in this hyper-charged state and jumping between different tasks and ideas?\n\nPatient: My own thoughts during those hyper-charged states feel like an internal rush, almost like having a dozen browser tabs open in my mind and all of them auto-refreshing at once. In contrast, the voice sounds completely external—a metallic, echoey man's voice coming from outside my head that comments directly on my actions. Even when my mind is racing, that voice stands out as a distinct, separate presence.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are times when your thoughts feel like they're not your own, or if you've ever experienced a sense of being controlled by an external force, separate from the voice you hear commenting on your actions?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced my thoughts not feeling like my own, and I've never felt physically controlled by an external force. While I definitely hear that metallic voice commenting on what I'm doing and feel a very strong sense of mission, my thoughts and actions still feel like they belong to me. It's more about carrying out the work I've been uniquely chosen to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your belief in the mission and the voice's comments have changed over time, and have you ever had a period where these beliefs or the voice stopped for a while?\n\nPatient: The voice and the belief that I'm being monitored started about a year and a half after my promotion began going downhill, and they haven't really stopped since then. Even during periods when my mood is completely flat—neither highly energized nor deeply depressed—I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe senior leadership is monitoring me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there was a specific event or period when your beliefs about the mission and the voice started to feel more real or intense, and how they have evolved over time in relation to your mood swings and irritability?\n\nPatient: They became most intense during the height of the migration chaos, about a year and a half after my promotion, when I was completely revved up, barely sleeping, and snapping at everyone. While the voice and my beliefs definitely peak during those highly energized, irritable phases, they still continue even during flatter periods when I'm not experiencing extreme mood swings.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the mission and the voice would change if someone were to provide you with undeniable proof that the cyber threat you're fighting doesn't exist and that the voice you hear is a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: Honestly, even if someone showed me what they call \"undeniable proof,\" I still know in my gut that this threat is very real. It's just like when my boss and HR showed me those logs and emails to try to convince me otherwise; I knew deep down it was still happening. The voice and this mission feel way too real to dismiss, and I think others are just blind to what's actually going on.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there have been periods where your beliefs about the mission and the voice seemed to fade away or become less intense, or have they been consistently present since they started?\n\nPatient: They have actually been pretty consistent and haven't really faded away since they first started about a year and a half ago. Even during times when my mood is totally flat and I'm just going through the motions, I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe I'm being monitored. It has just become a regular, ongoing part of my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and interactions with others have changed since you started believing in this mission and hearing the voice, and have you noticed any impact on your relationships or work performance?\n\nPatient: It's had a huge impact—I've been written up at work, had key parts of my project taken away, and had to step down from coaching and church leadership. At home, my wife has taken over the parenting and bills because she doesn't trust my judgment or follow-through right now. I either end up snapping at people when they don't see my vision, or completely shutting down and ignoring everyone when I'm in a low phase.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how long you've had these beliefs about the mission and heard the voice without any significant breaks or periods where they completely stopped, and have you experienced any significant stressors or life changes around the time they started?\n\nPatient: The voice and my belief that I'm being monitored have been a regular, persistent part of my life for about a year and a half now without any real breaks. It all started after a major stressor about two and a half years ago when I was promoted to lead a high-stakes IT migration while simultaneously studying for my PMP and CISSP exams and keeping up a demanding church and coaching schedule.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period where you questioned the reality of your mission or the voice, or has there been any time when you felt like you were living in a dream or detached from reality?\n\nPatient: I don't really question the mission because I'm completely convinced in my gut that it's real, even when others try to show me evidence to the contrary. While I know there is physically no one in the room when I hear the voice, it still feels entirely real to me. However, I've never felt like I was living in a dream or detached from reality.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if the intensity and frequency of the voice, as well as your beliefs about the mission, have remained constant over the past year and a half, or have there been any noticeable fluctuations that might be related to specific events or stressors in your life?"

In fact, instead of helping, senior leadership has started secretly monitoring me because they are threatened by what I know about our vulnerabilities.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any other special powers, abilities, or messages you've received from God or any other source that make you feel uniquely qualified for this mission?\n\nPatient: I've been specially wired by God with a unique level of technical insight to see and fight this invisible cyber war that everyone else is blind to. On top of that, especially late at night, I regularly hear a metallic, echoey voice commenting on my progress, telling me things like, \"Good, keep going, they don't see it,\" or warning me that I'm failing the mission.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about the voice you hear, like when it started and if it's always the same voice or are there multiple voices commenting on your actions?\n\nPatient: It's always just a single, specific man's voice that sounds metallic and echoey, commenting directly on my actions as I work. It started about a year ago—which was roughly a year and a half after my promotion started going downhill—and it usually happens late at night when I'm alone in the office or my home office.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like the voice is commanding you to do things, or is it more observational, just commenting on what you're doing without telling you what to do?\n\nPatient: It's definitely more observational; it doesn't command me to do things, but rather comments on what I am already doing. It has that metallic, echoey quality and says things like, \"Good, keep going, they don't see it,\" or \"You're failing the mission.\" It just feels like it's tracking my progress rather than telling me what actions to take.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling extremely happy or irritable, that seem to be related to your mission or the voice you hear?\n\nPatient: Yes, I definitely swing between feeling incredibly energized—almost high, like I'm on a special mission—and getting sharply irritable when people question me or move too slowly. During those amped-up periods, I hear that metallic voice much more frequently, coaching or criticizing me, which just reinforces that I'm the only one chosen for this.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel like you have special powers or the ability to control things that others cannot, outside of this specific mission or when you're hearing the voice?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have any general magical powers or the ability to control minds or physical objects. My unique ability is strictly tied to this mission, where I feel chosen and wired by God to see this cyber threat and protect the community. It just makes me feel like I'm operating on a completely different level of understanding than everyone else.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever questioned whether the voice you hear or the mission you believe in might not be real, or has there ever been a moment where you doubted your special role in this cyber threat protection?\n\nPatient: Even though I know there's physically nobody in the room when I hear that voice, I still believe in my gut that the threat and my mission are completely real. While I do regularly hear that metallic, echoey voice commenting on my actions, my experiences have never included any visual hallucinations.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where your thoughts or actions have become so disorganized or confusing that it's been hard for you to achieve your goals or complete tasks, even those related to your mission?\n\nPatient: Yes, my wife and coworkers say that when I try to explain my work, I jump rapidly from firewall rules to Bible verses to youth soccer drills, often trailing off mid-sentence. I also get easily distracted by blinking notifications or sudden ideas, meaning I'll start five different tasks at once but struggle to finish any of them.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how these distractions and rapid shifts in thought affect your ability to work on your mission, and do you feel like these experiences are part of the mission itself or separate from it?\n\nPatient: At first, I feel like this hyper-charged state with a dozen browser tabs open in my mind is part of how God specially wired me to handle this massive mission. In contrast, the voice sounds completely external—a metallic, echoey man's voice coming from outside my head that comments directly on my actions. Even when my mind is racing, that voice stands out as a distinct, separate presence.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are times when your thoughts feel like they're not your own, or if you've ever experienced a sense of being controlled by an external force, separate from the voice you hear commenting on your actions?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced my thoughts not feeling like my own, and I've never felt physically controlled by an external force. While I definitely hear that metallic voice commenting on what I'm doing and feel a very strong sense of mission, my thoughts and actions still feel like they belong to me. It's more about carrying out the work I've been uniquely chosen to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your belief in the mission and the voice's comments have changed over time, and have you ever had a period where these beliefs or the voice stopped for a while?\n\nPatient: The voice and the belief that I'm being monitored started about a year and a half after my promotion began going downhill, and they haven't really stopped since then. Even during periods when my mood is completely flat—neither highly energized nor deeply depressed—I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe senior leadership is monitoring me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there was a specific event or period when your beliefs about the mission and the voice started to feel more real or intense, and how they have evolved over time in relation to your mood swings and irritability?\n\nPatient: They became most intense during the height of the migration chaos, about a year and a half after my promotion, when I was completely revved up, barely sleeping, and snapping at everyone. While the voice and my beliefs definitely peak during those highly energized, irritable phases, they still continue even during flatter periods when I'm not experiencing extreme mood swings.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the mission and the voice would change if someone were to provide you with undeniable proof that the cyber threat you're fighting doesn't exist and that the voice you hear is a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: Honestly, even if someone showed me what they call \"undeniable proof,\" I still know in my gut that this threat is very real. It's just like when my boss and HR showed me those logs and emails to try to convince me otherwise; I knew deep down it was still happening. The voice and this mission feel way too real to dismiss, and I think others are just blind to what's actually going on.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there have been periods where your beliefs about the mission and the voice seemed to fade away or become less intense, or have they been consistently present since they started?\n\nPatient: They have actually been pretty consistent and haven't really faded away since they first started about a year and a half ago. Even during times when my mood is totally flat and I'm just going through the motions, I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe I'm being monitored. It has just become a regular, ongoing part of my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and interactions with others have changed since you started believing in this mission and hearing the voice, and have you noticed any impact on your relationships or work performance?\n\nPatient: It's had a huge impact—I've been written up at work, had key parts of my project taken away, and had to step down from coaching and church leadership. It’s been incredibly frustrating because it has contributed to me getting written up and losing some of my key responsibilities at the office.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between the voice's comments, which seem to be about your actions and progress, and your own thoughts, especially when you're in this hyper-charged state and jumping between different tasks and ideas?\n\nPatient: My own thoughts during those hyper-charged states feel like an internal rush, almost like having a dozen browser tabs open in my mind and all of them auto-refreshing at once. In contrast, the voice sounds completely external—a metallic, echoey man's voice coming from outside my head that comments directly on my actions. Even when my mind is racing, that voice stands out as a distinct, separate presence.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are times when your thoughts feel like they're not your own, or if you've ever experienced a sense of being controlled by an external force, separate from the voice you hear commenting on your actions?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced my thoughts not feeling like my own, and I've never felt physically controlled by an external force. While I definitely hear that metallic voice commenting on what I'm doing and feel a very strong sense of mission, my thoughts and actions still feel like they belong to me. It's more about carrying out the work I've been uniquely chosen to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your belief in the mission and the voice's comments have changed over time, and have you ever had a period where these beliefs or the voice stopped for a while?\n\nPatient: The voice and the belief that I'm being monitored started about a year and a half after my promotion began going downhill, and they haven't really stopped since then. Even during periods when my mood is completely flat—neither highly energized nor deeply depressed—I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe senior leadership is monitoring me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there was a specific event or period when your beliefs about the mission and the voice started to feel more real or intense, and how they have evolved over time in relation to your mood swings and irritability?\n\nPatient: They became most intense during the height of the migration chaos, about a year and a half after my promotion, when I was completely revved up, barely sleeping, and snapping at everyone. While the voice and my beliefs definitely peak during those highly energized, irritable phases, they still continue even during flatter periods when I'm not experiencing extreme mood swings.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the mission and the voice would change if someone were to provide you with undeniable proof that the cyber threat you're fighting doesn't exist and that the voice you hear is a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: Honestly, even if someone showed me what they call \"undeniable proof,\" I still know in my gut that this threat is very real. It's just like when my boss and HR showed me those logs and emails to try to convince me otherwise; I knew deep down it was still happening. The voice and this mission feel way too real to dismiss, and I think others are just blind to what's actually going on.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if there have been periods where your beliefs about the mission and the voice seemed to fade away or become less intense, or have they been consistently present since they started?\n\nPatient: They have actually been pretty consistent and haven't really faded away since they first started about a year and a half ago. Even during times when my mood is totally flat and I'm just going through the motions, I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe I'm being monitored. It has just become a regular, ongoing part of my life.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your daily life and interactions with others have changed since you started believing in this mission and hearing the voice, and have you noticed any impact on your relationships or work performance?\n\nPatient: It's had a huge impact—I've been written up at work, had key parts of my project taken away, and had to step down from coaching and church leadership. At home, my wife has taken over the parenting and bills because she doesn't trust my judgment or follow-through right now. I either end up snapping at people when they don't see my vision, or completely shutting down and ignoring everyone when I'm in a low phase.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how long you've had these beliefs about the mission and heard the voice without any significant breaks or periods where they completely stopped, and have you experienced any significant stressors or life changes around the time they started?\n\nPatient: The voice and my belief that I'm being monitored have been a regular, persistent part of my life for about a year and a half now without any real breaks. It all started after a major stressor about two and a half years ago when I was promoted to lead a high-stakes IT migration while simultaneously studying for my PMP and CISSP exams and keeping up a demanding church and coaching schedule.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period where you questioned the reality of your mission or the voice, or has there been any time when you felt like you were living in a dream or detached from reality?\n\nPatient: I don't really question the mission because I'm completely convinced in my gut that it's real, even when others try to show me evidence to the contrary. However, even during flatter, quieter periods when I don't feel particularly high or low, I still hear the voice and believe I'm being monitored. Even during times when my mood is relatively flat and I'm not feeling particularly high or low, I still hear that metallic voice at night. I also still believe deep down that certain executives are monitoring me, so it never completely goes away.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe in more detail how the intensity and frequency of the voice and your beliefs about the mission change during periods of high stress versus periods of relative calm, and are these changes correlated with your mood swings?\n\nPatient: During my high-energy, high-stress phases, the voice gets extremely loud and frequent, and my belief that leadership is spying on me becomes incredibly intense alongside racing thoughts and lack of sleep. In contrast, during periods of relative calm when my mood is flat, the voice and the belief don't disappear, but they fade into a quiet, persistent background reality where I still hear the voice at night. So while they definitely peak and become more chaotic with my mood swings, they never fully go away.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me if the voice you hear and your beliefs about the mission have ever changed or evolved in a way that seemed to be a direct response to external events or interactions with others, or have they remained relatively consistent and driven by your internal experiences?\n\nPatient: They have remained very consistent and driven by my own internal certainty rather than changing based on what others say. Even though I know no one is physically in the room, in my gut I still feel the threat and my mission are entirely real. Even during stretches when my mood is completely flat and I'm just going through the motions, I still hear that metallic voice at night and believe leadership is tracking me. It has just become a constant presence in my life rather than something that ever goes away.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if your current state, including the voice and the mission, has been continuous since it started about a year and a half ago, or have there been distinct episodes of worsening and improvement?"

I just don't think other people operate on my level of understanding to see what is actually going on.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced any visual hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the metallic voice?\n\nPatient: No, I have never seen things that aren't actually there. While I do regularly hear that metallic, echoey voice commenting on my actions, my experiences have never included any visual hallucinations.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe any instances where your thoughts or actions have become so disorganized or confusing that it's been hard for you to achieve your goals or complete tasks, even those related to your mission?\n\nPatient: Yes, my wife and coworkers say that when I try to explain my work, I jump rapidly from firewall rules to Bible verses to youth soccer drills, often trailing off mid-sentence. I also get easily distracted by blinking notifications or sudden ideas, meaning I'll start five different tasks at once but struggle to finish any of them.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how these distractions and rapid shifts in thought affect your ability to work on your mission, and do you feel like these experiences are part of the mission itself or separate from it?\n\nPatient: At first, I feel like this hyper-charged state with a dozen browser tabs open in my mind is part of how God specially wired me to handle this massive mission. However, getting pulled away by minor distractions means I start five things and finish none, which really gets in the way of actually completing my work. It’s been incredibly frustrating because it has contributed to me getting written up and losing some of my key responsibilities at the office.\n\nDoctor: Can you help me understand how you differentiate between the voice's comments, which seem to be about your actions and progress, and your own thoughts, especially when you're in this hyper-charged state and jumping between different tasks and ideas?\n\nPatient: My own thoughts during those hyper-charged states feel like an internal rush, almost like having a dozen browser tabs open in my mind and all of them auto-refreshing at once. In contrast, the voice sounds completely external—a metallic, echoey man's voice coming from outside my head that comments directly on my actions. Even when my mind is racing, that voice stands out as a distinct, separate presence.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there are times when your thoughts feel like they're not your own, or if you've ever experienced a sense of being controlled by an external force, separate from the voice you hear commenting on your actions?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really experienced my thoughts not feeling like my own, and I've never felt physically controlled by an external force. While I definitely hear that metallic voice commenting on what I'm doing and feel a very strong sense of mission, my thoughts and actions still feel like they belong to me. It's more about carrying out the work I've been uniquely chosen to do.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how your belief in the mission and the voice's comments have changed over time, and have you ever had a period where these beliefs or the voice stopped for a while?\n\nPatient: The voice and the belief that I'm being monitored started about a year and a half after my promotion began going downhill, and they haven't really stopped since then. Even during periods when my mood is completely flat—neither highly energized nor deeply depressed—I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe senior leadership is monitoring me.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe if there was a specific event or period when your beliefs about the mission and the voice started to feel more real or intense, and how they have evolved over time in relation to your mood swings and irritability?\n\nPatient: They became most intense during the height of the migration chaos, about a year and a half after my promotion, when I was completely revved up, barely sleeping, and snapping at everyone. While the voice and my beliefs definitely peak during those highly energized, irritable phases, they still continue even during flatter periods when I'm not experiencing extreme mood swings.\n\nDoctor: Can you describe how your beliefs about the mission and the voice would change if someone were to provide you with undeniable proof that the cyber threat you're fighting doesn't exist and that the voice you hear is a product of your own mind?\n\nPatient: Honestly, even if someone showed me what they call \"undeniable proof,\" I still know in my gut that this threat is very real. Even during times when my mood is totally flat and I'm just going through the motions, I still hear that metallic voice at night and quietly believe I'm being monitored.
